newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Magalhaes to remain Brazil chief whip - presidency.
newsitem.headline: Magalhaes to remain Brazil chief whip - presidency.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Brazilian president Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Wednesday the government's chief whip in the lower house of Congress Deputy Luis Eduardo Magalhaes would remain in his job.
"The president asked him to stay, and he will remain leader," the spokeswoman said, squelching reports earlier today that Magalhaes was about to resign.

Magalhaes was reportedly furious at comments by controversial Communications Minister Sergio Motta, who in a recent interview criticized several political parties that make up the government's alliance in Congress.
Magalhaes is one of the most important members of the Liberal Front Party (PFL), the government's closest ally and its most enthusiastic supporter in economic and structural reform.
Magalhaes met with Cardoso at the Planalto Palace earlier today, but drove off without making any comment to reporters awaiting word on his status.

Prices on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange, which had slumped over three percent earlier on the reports, rebounded swiftly on the palace's announcement. The key Bovespa index erased its losses and jumped 3.44 percent.
